Chapter 1: The Evolution of Modern Architecture

Architecture is both the process and the product of planning, designing, and constructing buildings or other structures. Architectural works, in the material form of buildings, are often perceived as cultural symbols and as works of art. Historical civilizations are often identified with their surviving architectural achievements.

The practice, which began in the Neolithic era, has been used to express culture across several global civilizations. Since ancient times, the primary need has been shelter, security, and worship, evolving into complex urban planning and aesthetic expression.

In contemporary design, sustainability and human-centric spaces take center stage. Architects must balance environmental impact with structural integrity, utilizing advanced composite materials and smart automation systems to optimize energy consumption.

As cities expand vertically and transit networks interconnect populations globally, the psychological comfort of travelers and commuters has become a prominent field of study. Integrating real-time sensory adaptation tools ensures that technological advancements directly improve daily human well-being during transit.
